prompt_en: Create a landscape visible-light operational documentary photograph inside a crowded orbital-station module during a scheduled inspection. Microgravity is made visible through simultaneous unsupported floating, divergent orientations, and handrail-based motion control. This is a microgravity station interior with unsupported multi-orientation floating. An original visibly adult station specialist floats diagonally with both feet visibly clear of every surface while hooked fingertips arrest motion on a handrail. The specialist's readable face shape, eye appearance, lower-face shape, hairline, and long dark wavy hair follow the attached portrait as appearance-only reference. At least three loose objects float unsupported at different angles; one pouch is upside down relative to the specialist. In the same frame, station-module racks handrails and stowage establish a real orbital interior; multiple bodies or loose objects float without visible support or ballistic jumping cues; subjects and objects occupy different orientations with no shared downward direction; hands feet or restraints engage rails and loops to control motion. A wide full-body frame keeps the referenced face, free feet, rail contact, and three objects readable. Practical cabin LEDs illuminate face, hand contact, hardware, and objects with documentary clarity.
